post.caption: A ten pound ring hid a diamond. In the 1980s, a woman paid ten pounds for a ring at a car boot sale in west London. She thought it was costume jewelry and wore it for years. In 2017, a local jeweler suspected the stone was a diamond and sent her to Sotheby's. The Gemological Institute of America graded it at 26.27 carats. Sotheby's called it the Tenner and estimated up to 350,000 pounds. It sold in London on June 7, 2017, for 656,750 pounds, nearly double the estimate.
